title: APT Package Manifest
description: Defines Debian packages to build from source or download from system repositories.

entries.description: List of APT packages to manage.

name.description: Logical package name used in logs and the TUI.

version.description: Package version. Used in build paths and S3 keys to allow multiple versions.

source_name.description: Upstream package or directory name. Defaults to name when absent. This is the name 'apt-get download' asks for, so it is the binary package name.

source_package.description: Debian source package this binary was built from, as dpkg reports it in ${source:Package}. Read by the OSV gate, because Ubuntu and Debian advisories are issued against the source. Absent means no capture recorded one, which is not the same as equal to name.

capture_suite.description: Release the host this version was captured on was running, as 'bodega pkg convert apt' records it from --suite or /etc/os-release. Read by the OSV gate, which keys a distro advisory on the release because Ubuntu and Debian backport a fix without moving the upstream version. Ignored by the index generator: suites decides where the .deb is published, and on a server whose apt_codename is a local name the two are different values.

url.description: Git URL to clone for a source build. When omitted, the package is fetched via apt-get download.

build_cmd.description: Shell command to run from the package root (cloned source directory). The working directory is the repo root, so 'build-deb.sh' is sufficient — no './' prefix needed.

deb_glob.description: Glob pattern (relative to source dir) to locate the built .deb file.

suites.description: APT suites (dists/<suite>/) this package is published to. Absent means the server's default suite (config apt_codename). Suite names must not contain "/".

frozen.description: When true, the entry cannot be built, edited, or deleted.

storage.description: Name of the storage backend holding this version's artifact bytes. Absent means "default" — the backend defined by storage_backend/storage_path/bucket/region — and is correct for every artifact uploaded before named backends existed. It is not a placement rule: storage_by_type decides where the next write goes, this records where an already-written artifact is.
